# ADR-0000: Template

**Status:** Template — copy, do not edit in place.

Statuses in use: `Proposed` · `Accepted` · `Pending — <checkpoint>` · `Superseded by ADR-XXXX`.

An ADR that deviates from a locked specification document must say so explicitly
in its Status line, e.g. `Accepted — supersedes Tech.md §4.3`. The specification
files themselves stay byte-identical; this index is how a reader of a superseded
section finds what overrode it.

---

## Context

What forced a decision. The constraint, the conflict, or the thing that turned
out not to work. Enough that someone who wasn't there can reconstruct the
pressure without reading the whole history.

## Decision

What we do. Stated in the present tense, as a rule rather than a narrative.

## Alternatives considered

Each with the reason it lost. This section is the difference between an ADR that
states a decision and one that lets you re-evaluate it later — a rejected option
whose rejection reason has expired is exactly what you want to find.

## Consequences

What this makes easy, what it makes hard, and what now has to stay true. Include
the cost of reversing it.

## References

Questionnaire items (`docs/decisions/p0-questionnaire.md`) this derives from, and
any spec sections it touches.
